If you're in SEM or SEO area, this may make more sense.

Basically, I think I've found a way to get individual keyword analytics (e.g. time on site, pages / visit, bounce rate, etc) from Google / Bing / etc. on organic search. What that means is when someone types in "flowers" into google and clicks a non-ad link, I can tell that website analytics about that keyword such as avg Time on Site, Bounce Rate, etc.

Back story: whenever a person visits a site, they have an HTTP_REFERER header saying where they are coming from (side note: don't go from pornhub to facebook as facebook will now know you were just on pornhub). Anyways, when a user used to search for something on Google (e.g. roses) then their http_referer header would be set to something like "google.com?q=roses&otherInfoHere" where you can then parse the Q parameter and then track that user to determine analytics for each keyword.

Around 2012, Google disabled this feature for organic search (not for ads, just organic) so the http_referer basically became "google.com". Now you can't tie the keyword to the user and hence you cannot get analytics about that given keyword. You can still determine that from "google.com" as a whole you are getting X on TimeOnSite & a 30% bounce rate, but that's your overall average rather than on a keyword-basis.

Low and behold, I'm 90% sure I've found a way to fix this where you can get back your analytics on a keyword basis. This has two major implications: SEM (search engine marketing): if you know what kind of conversions you're getting w/ organic keywords then you can position your budget early on for the keywords that are working. SEO (search engine optimization): obviously you can now determine which keywords are performing and start to optimize for them more.

However, any feedback would be awesome!
